title: POC scoping - Data handling / Vitality Health
next_steps: Samira to share SOC2 + security datasheet
Ethan to run 10k-token throughput benchmark on a sample dataset and share results
Customer to provide 2 weeks of representative logs and 50 anonymized prompts by 2027-03-27
action_items: Samira: send SOC2, ISO docs and the redwood security deck by 2027-03-22
Ethan: run latency/throughput benchmarks (1k, 5k, 10k tokens) on Redwood Dedicated sizing options and upload spreadsheet by 2027-03-26
Priya: share PII samples and expected retention windows by 2027-03-25
summary: POC scope focused on data handling: PII, logging/redaction, retention, prompt storage. Discussed success criteria (latency, accuracy, no PII leakage), workload sizing and benchmark plan, and timeline for a 3-week POC. Security and compliance requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO) emphasized; Redwood to provide security docs and run benchmarks on Dedicated and Hosted options.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through POC scope - mostly data handling concerns. um Ethan is on to cover benchmarks.
[00:06] Dr. Aaron Kim: thanks Samira, quick intro — we're trying to evaluate Redwood for powering our clinical summarization pipeline, main concerns are PII, audit logs, and retention policies.
[00:18] Priya Shah: security lead here, hi, we need to make sure PHI doesn't leak to logs or third-party models, and key management is enterprise-grade.
[00:27] Ethan Liu: yeah, great. quick note: we typically offer three deployment modes — Redwood Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For POC we usually run on Dedicated or Private depending on networking.
[00:41] Daniel Ortega: network wise we prefer VPC peering or Private with our KMS. Latency targets are sub-300ms for 256-token replies, throughput ~50 qps sustained for the ingest side. Is that realistic?
[00:55] Maya Rodriguez: 50 qps sustained with 256-token outputs is achievable on a modest Dedicated pool; depends on model variant and quantization. we should capture expected burst patterns.
[01:07] Laura Finch: success criteria for us: 1) no PII persisted in raw form, 2) avg latency < 300ms p95, 3) F1/ROUGE-like accuracy degradation < 3% vs baseline, and 4) clear audit trail for compliance.
[01:23] Samira Patel: solid. on PII, we support request-level redaction and optional prompt stripping before storage. we can also configure retention windows per-tenant — e.g., 0 days (no logging), 7/30/90 days, or retain only anonymized transcripts.
[01:38] Priya Shah: how does redaction work? is it automatic or pattern-based? any ML false-negatives risk?
[01:45] Ethan Liu: two modes: deterministic redaction using regex and rule-based scrubbing for SSNs, MRNs, phone numbers, plus an ML-assisted entity detector for names/addresses. we recommend combining both; ML helps catch context-sensitive PII but we keep the original raw text only if customer opts in and we encrypt-at-rest with their KMS key.
[02:05] Dr. Aaron Kim: can you guarantee original prompts won't be stored as part of the model cache or telemetry?
[02:12] Maya Rodriguez: yes, by default we do prefix caching (KV cache) in runtime but that's in-memory and not persisted to logs. however if you enable session replay or longer retention, prompt text may be stored unless redaction is applied before ingest. we can also disable prompt storage entirely for POC — then logs will only have metadata/trace ids.
[02:34] Daniel Ortega: great, but what about RL or model-training telemetry? we can't have customer prompts used for training.
[02:40] Samira Patel: Redwood does not use customer data to train public models. for Hosted customers we have opt-in analytics, and for Dedicated/Private, data never leaves the customer's environment unless you enable sharing; we'll add contract language.
[02:55] Priya Shah: KMS and HSM — we need CMEK for keys, rotation policy, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:02] Ethan Liu: we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSMs in Private mode. we can configure CMEK for at-rest encryption and wire it into your vault; audit logs are exportable via syslog/S3 or CloudWatch depending on deployment.
[03:18] Laura Finch: logging retention — default logs are 90 days, but for POC we want a 7-day retention with redaction applied immediately. is that configurable per-route?
[03:27] Maya Rodriguez: yes, per-route retention and redaction policies are supported in Redwood Console. we'll show how to set that in the POC.
[03:34] Dr. Aaron Kim: benchmark plan? we need throughput and p95 numbers across our 3 payload shapes: short prompts (32 tokens in/out), medium (256), and long-form (1k+).
[03:45] Ethan Liu: plan proposed: run synthetic benchmarks at 1k, 5k, and 10k concurrent requests over 15-minute windows for each payload shape, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and GPU utilization. we'll include cold-start and warmed KV-cache runs.
[04:00] Samira Patel: and we'll compare Hosted vs Dedicated cost estimates and have Redwood suggest batching and quantization profiles to meet cost/latency targets.
[04:09] Daniel Ortega: timeline — we want POC to be 3 weeks: week1 integration + security review, week2 benchmark runs, week3 analysis and executive review. is that workable?
[04:19] Maya Rodriguez: yes, that's our typical cadence. we'll need access (API key or VPC peering) and representative samples by Friday to start week1.
[04:27] Priya Shah: one more: prompt storage concerns — for debugging we need some prompts, but PHI must be redacted. can we store hashed prompt ids and anonymized examples only?
[04:36] Ethan Liu: absolutely. we can store a prompt-id hash and a redacted snippet, and keep full bodies disabled. the Console shows token-level cost without exposing raw content.
[04:46] Dr. Aaron Kim: what's the expected size of logs/retention impact on cost?
[04:50] Samira Patel: depends on retention window and whether full text stored. rough rule — storing redacted transcripts costs ~0.1x of token compute; full transcripts increase storage costs and may trigger higher egress accounting. We'll provide a cost sketch in the spreadsheet.
[05:05] Laura Finch: legal/procurement — what's needed to allow Dedicated access? any lengthy paperwork?
[05:10] Samira Patel: for Dedicated typically a standard contract and an order form; for Private (VPC/on-prem) we add an MSA with security annex. We'll surface contract checklist.
[05:18] Priya Shah: audit trail — need per-request audit id, who/what accessed logs, and immutability for 90 days.
[05:24] Ethan Liu: per-request tracing is generated automatically; audit exports can be forwarded to your SIEM with S3 signatures for immutability.
[05:31] Daniel Ortega: any gotchas with KV cache and PII — could a name from prior session persist in cache and get used in a different session?
[05:38] Maya Rodriguez: KV cache keys are per-session by default. for multi-tenant setups we namespace caches. for safety we also provide cache eviction on session end. we'll show the default eviction policy and how to set strict session isolation.
[05:52] Dr. Aaron Kim: benchmarks — please include accuracy regressions check vs our baseline summarizer, not just latency.
[05:58] Ethan Liu: yes, we'll run the model on a labeled eval set and compute ROUGE/F1 differences; that'll be in the benchmark report.
[06:06] Samira Patel: ok, recap of next steps: Samira share SOC2/security pack; Ethan run synthetic benchmarks and labeled eval; customer provide sample prompts and PII examples; schedule follow-up 2027-03-30 for results.
[06:18] Laura Finch: thanks all, sounds good.
[06:20] Samira Patel: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and the benchmark template.
[06:25] (call ends)
